note.after_visit_summary: Your child had an asthma flare-up likely triggered by a recent cold, which got worse because his daily controller medicine (fluticasone) was stopped. In the clinic, we gave a breathing treatment that helped his oxygen and breathing. We started a short course of oral steroid (prednisolone) to reduce lung inflammation. He should take prednisolone 30 mg (10 mL of the liquid) once daily for 5 days. For quick relief, use albuterol 4 puffs with a spacer every 4 hours while awake for the next 2 days, then only as needed. Restart the daily fluticasone inhaler: 2 puffs twice a day, every day, even when he feels well—have him rinse his mouth after each use to prevent throat irritation. We’ve updated his asthma action plan and sent a copy to his school nurse. He can return to school when he doesn’t need albuterol more than every 4 hours. Watch for warning signs: needing albuterol more than every 4 hours, trouble speaking in full sentences, visible pulling in of the ribs with breathing, or bluish lips—if any of these occur, go to the emergency room. Follow up with us this Friday to check his progress and give his flu shot. Keep using the same pharmacy and insurance (member ID M as in Mary 6 6 2 0 4 1 8). Call us at 555-0129 with any questions.
